title: Testimony service
hook: church members stand and tell what God has done this week

segments.voice: Yesterday, the prayer meeting: honest, hopeful prayers for the people behind each door. Your line was prayer changes things. Which door did you do something for? Day one thousand one hundred seventy-six.

A man who lived among the tombs, breaking every chain they put on him and crying out in the hills, is sitting by the lake now, clothed and calm. Mark's Gospel tells it. Jesus has set him free, and as Jesus climbs back into the boat, the man begs to come along. It's an understandable request. And Jesus says no. He says: "Go home to thy friends, and tell them how great things the Lord hath done for thee, and hath had compassion on thee." So the man goes home and tells it, all over his region. Not a sermon. A report. That's the heart of today's room: the testimony service, where church members stand up and tell what God has done this week.
screen: `A MAN BY THE LAKE, CLOTHED AND CALM.`

segments.voice: A psalm sets the pattern: "Come and hear, all ye that fear God, and I will declare what he hath done for my soul." The psalmist doesn't argue. He tells. In Black churches and Pentecostal churches, the testimony service makes room for exactly that. The floor opens, and one after another, people stand. Some begin with a familiar opening, giving honor to God, and then the story comes. A job found. A test result. A son who called after a long silence. A hard week that didn't break them. Sometimes just: I woke up this morning. And the room answers each one, the way it answered the preacher, with amen and thank you, Jesus. Today's line is a sentence you may hear at the center of it: God has been good. The Book of Revelation gives testimony real weight. It says of the faithful: "they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony." There it's the witness of the faithful under pressure, and some who testify on a Sunday hear their own small reports in that line. Today closes a week, so look back at the rooms we've walked through. Praise, hands raised. A hand on a shoulder and a prayer. A word for someone, weighed. Bold prayer for the sick. The preacher calling and the people answering. The prayer meeting naming every need. And now the testimony. In every one of them, something is said out loud from the pews: a hallelujah, a prayer, a weighed word, an amen, a story.
screen: `I WILL DECLARE WHAT HE HATH DONE.`
`A WEEK OF ROOMS WHERE EVERYONE SPEAKS.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: find one good thing from your week. Settle, and breathe. Go back through the week a day at a time. Last night. The day before. The start of the week. Look for one good thing. It can be small: a conversation, a meal, a moment you were helped. When you find it, say it out loud in a sentence or two, plainly, as a report. This happened. If you pray, you can begin it with thanks. The bell holds the time.
Testimony service. A time in worship when members stand and tell, plainly, what God has done for them this week.
Your line: God has been good. Today, tell one person the good thing you found, in a sentence or two, without dressing it up. Day one thousand one hundred seventy-six.

howItsDone: In Black and Pentecostal churches, a part of the service or a midweek meeting is set aside for testimony: members stand, often beginning by giving honor to God, tell what God has done for them, and the congregation responds aloud.

notes: Week close (days 1170–1176): the look-back lists praise, laying on of hands, prophecy and discernment, praying for healing, call and response, the prayer meeting and testimony service.

Mark 5:1–20 paraphrased: the man among the tombs, chains (5:3–5), sitting clothed and in his right mind (5:15), begging to be with Jesus (5:18), publishing it in Decapolis (5:20). 'By the lake' and 'all over his region' summarize; confirm.
'Giving honor to God' as a common opening of testimonies is described as 'a familiar opening' used by some; confirm.
Original: μαρτυρία in Revelation 12:11 (τὸν λόγον τῆς μαρτυρίας αὐτῶν); confirm. No martyr etymology is claimed.

Audit pass (2026-10-02): 'A small report from a pew ... is counted as part of the fight' had the narrator extend Revelation 12:11 (the faithful overcoming the accuser, in a passage about martyrdom) to ordinary testimonies as if the text said so; now framed as how people who testify hear the line. 'Some who testify' is kept deliberately modest under the claims rule.

Editor pass: 'chained and unchained and screaming' (garbled) rewritten from Mark 5:3–5; 'often the sentence at the center' softened; the week's closing line changed from 'nobody comes only to watch', which repeated day 1174's 'nobody is just the audience', to a concrete list.
